title: Daily temperatures
prompt:
For each day, find how many days you have to wait until a strictly warmer day. If no warmer day comes, the answer for that day is 0. (PageTurn uses the same logic for "days until you read more than today".)

Write daysUntilWarmer(temps) that returns an array of the same length. Aim for O(n) time; scanning forward from every day is O(n²).

Examples:

  • daysUntilWarmer([73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73]) → [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]
  • daysUntilWarmer([30, 20, 25, 40, 10, 15, 50]) → [3, 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 0]
  • daysUntilWarmer([50, 50, 50]) → [0, 0, 0] (equal is not warmer)

Constraints: 0 ≤ temps.length ≤ 105, values can be negative.

tests.name: matches scanning forward on many small inputs

hints: "For each element, the next greater element to its right" is the monotonic stack trigger. Instead of each day looking forward, let each new day answer the earlier days that are still waiting.

Keep a stack of indexes of days that haven't found a warmer day yet. For each new day: while the stack isn't empty and today is warmer than the day on top, pop that day and set its answer to today - thatDay. Then push today.

Shape:

const answer = new Array(temps.length).fill(0);
const waiting = [];
for (let today = 0; today < temps.length; today++) {
  while (waiting.length > 0 && temps[today] > temps[waiting[waiting.length - 1]]) {
    const day = waiting.pop();
    answer[day] = today - day;
  }
  waiting.push(today);
}
return answer;
explain:
Time O(n), space O(n). Each index is pushed once and popped at most once, so all the inner while loops together do at most n pops. The forward-scan brute force is O(n²) on inputs like a long cool spell followed by one hot day.

The stack is monotonic: the temperatures of waiting days only decrease from bottom to top, because a warmer day would have popped any colder day below it.

In an interview: "This is next-greater-element, so I'll use a monotonic stack of indexes still waiting for a warmer day. Each new day pops every colder waiting day and records the distance. Every index is pushed and popped once: O(n) time, O(n) space."
